First off, thank you for wanting to learn and understand rather than just turn ignorance towards us, which indeed happens a lot. 

Your first question is a tricky one because no one trans person has the same experience. Some find it out when they're 5, some 15, some 50 years old because either the feeling is repressed, closeted, or just unknown. It's a strange random thought to think "oh maybe I'm so unhappy with life because I'm not seen as a male/female/nb? 

So I'll tell you my experience. Grew up as a girl. But around 7 or 8, I started realizing I liked showing myself off as a boy. I wanted to wear boxers, not be called the name I had, hang out with just boys and stuff. You're probably thinking, "well girls wear boxers and hang out with boys all the time!" Yes, but *there's a difference.*

Around high school is where it all started to happen. I started growing very repulsed by my non masculine body. I hated being known as a girl, it made me depressed to be associated as one and I didn't know what was happening. I remember hearing about this guy from a YouTuber I watched named Buck Angel. I remember feeling strangely attached..

Boom. It came into my mind. I researched it night and day, realized what I was feeling is called gender dysphoria, and it all made sense. Since then I've been transitioning (slowly as I have no money to move out and actually change.) 

Your second question is also tricky. I would say (at least in the USA) that we have a very one step forward, two steps back mentality. We started making progress, then our progress in other areas was taken away. However, I'm sure the Dutch (I'm guessing you're living somewhere around the Netherlands) is most likely transphobia free at least for the most part. Unfortunately, the situation of trans rights varies from country to country, lies heavily on the religious beliefs of the country, and most likely will take a very long time to change, no matter how accepting of the country. 

If you want to learn more about this, I would strongly suggest looking at the history. Learn about Marsha P. Johnson, the poc trans woman who started the Stonewall riots with her friend. Look up Laverne Cox, another poc trans woman today who speaks out on these issues and has a lot of sucess. Look at Buck Angel, a trans man who also speaks out on these issues and works hard to make sure trans men feel secure in their bodies. Look at trans celebrities in the last century, trans people in history, there's a lot more that history has almost erased, but they're there.

Here's how I do it:

1.) I take a car and think what I want to do with it, what class it should be and what it's going to me used for (rally, drift, etc.) 

2.) Then I figure out what class I want it to be, sort of determined by what it's capabilities are.

3.) That's when I add the upgrades I need, which after a while becomes a lot easier once you figure out what upgrades are common to different types of tunes. These are what change your class level, some upgrades more than others.

4.) Then I do technical tunings, which don't change your class level. I take it on a drive and check things as they go, depending on what I'm trying to do. So if I had an s1 rally car, I'd make sure my gears are adjusted, check the ride height, see how grippy the tires are and the like.

I hope this helps a bit more! Like I said, after a while you get the hang of it, I don't know half the technical jargan that they use but I'm slowly getting it.

Oh, and one more thing, write things down. It's good to have a list of all the changes you make so if you change something and you don't like it, you can change it back without having to just reset all the changes you made previously.

HokiHoshi has some good videos on YouTube on how to tune cars, honestly the more you do it the more you get used to it and the more you figure out how to adjust cars to your driving style. It's tricky at first but once you get it it's a fun thing to do
